To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IFN-γ response to Mtb antigens is lower in diabetic patients compared to those with normal glucose tolerance.
the IFN- γ release in TB patients and non-tB controls is associated with diabetes.
diabetes is associated with a reduction of Mtb-specific and mitogen-induced IFN-γ levels in TB patients and non-tB controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between diabetes and tuberculosis, which is a major public health problem in many countries.
the impact of diabetes on Mtb-specific IFNgamma responses in TB patients and non-tB controls from a high TB burden setting in Tanzania.
the association between diabetes status and the performance of IGRA for the diagnosis of LTBI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetes is associated with lower Mtb antigen-specific interferon release in Tanzanian TB patients and non TB controls.
diabetes is associated with reduced levels Mtb antigen-specific interferon-gamma release in a TB patient and non-TB control population from Tanzania.
diabetes is associated with reduced levels Mtb antigen-specific T-cell response, but the clinical relevance of this finding remains to be determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the IFN-γ test should be interpreted cautiously in individuals with diabetes, and that the IFN-gamma test may not be a suitable test to assess the risk of progression from LTBI to active TB in individuals with diabetes.
IFN- γ testing in diabetes patients may lead to an overestimation of LTBI prevalence, and thus an overestimation in the need for TB preventive therapy.
diabetes is associated with lower Mtb antigen-specific interferon-gamma release in both TB patients and non-tb controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diabetes is associated with a reduction in IFN-γ release to both Mtb and mitogen antigens, and this association does not depend on the TB status of the participant.
IGRA results may be compromised in individuals with diabetes, and that diabetes should be taken into account when interpreting IGRA results in the context of TB screening.
diabetes may be associated with reduced IFN- γ release and that this may have implications for the use of IGRA tests for LTBI in individuals with diabetes.
